verdicts.why: As a mode of travel, 'by air' names the means plainly and takes no attitude toward it.
The classical element is a technical, historical label with no judgement in it.
A school's presiding officer is a plain title of office, like 'head' or 'principal'.
Being able to defeat rivals is the meaning itself, a strong meaning rather than an attitude added on top of it.
A degree-holder is a plain academic status with nothing judged.
The licensed commander of a merchant ship is a plain occupational title.
A master key is a plain name for an object, with no attitude toward it.
The original recording from which copies are made is a plain technical term.
Compensation for a wrong is a formal, plain naming of the remedy; the word takes no side about it.
The legal payment of a debt is a plain term of art with no judgement.
A petit mal seizure is an unpleasant referent named in a neutral clinical word.
Direction in time, order or degree is described without any attitude.
Toward the bow is a plain nautical direction.
A reason for wanting something done is named plainly, without approval or contempt for the wanting.
A legal share or financial involvement is a plain term of law and finance.
A pleasant diversion is named without the speaker judging the pastime or the person who has it.

'The interests' controlling a field often lands as faintly adversarial, hinting at self-serving power, but in plain reporting it is also a neutral collective label; I cannot settle which is the word's own doing.
To use up resources is a plain statement of consumption with no attitude toward it.
Dance as an art form is named plainly, with no judgement of it.
The general atmosphere of a place is described neutrally; any judgement comes from the modifier, not from 'look'.
An anxious feeling is an unpleasant referent, but 'care' names it plainly, without belittling or dramatising the one who feels it.
Maintenance activity is named plainly and without attitude.
A cause for concern is a bad referent in a plain word; the word itself takes no side.
A decorative or artistic work is named plainly, with no judgement of its quality.
A preliminary sketch is a plain descriptive term with no attitude in it.
